Download a file with live progress

Source: R/download_progress.R
bricklayer_download.Rd

Downloads one file from the web to a local path, showing a progress bar (percent, size and rate) while a person is watching. It is the single download routine of the package and its sibling packages, and it applies the package's network safety rules: HTTPS only, no local or private addresses, a size cap, and checked redirects. Use it when a script must fetch a source file and you want a visible, safe transfer.

Usage

bricklayer_download(
  url,
  dest,
  headers = NULL,
  label = basename(dest),
  size = NULL,
  timeout = 3600,
  quiet = NULL,
  tty = NULL,
  allow_file = FALSE,
  max_bytes = 2^31
)

Arguments

url

The URL: https (plain http only with options(rmoriebricklayer.allow_http = TRUE)); a loopback, link-local or private address is refused.

dest

Character string: the path to write.

headers

Character vector of request headers, every element named (name = header, value = its value), or NULL (the default).

label

Text shown in front of the bar; the file name by default.

size

Expected size in bytes when known (a percent bar instead of a spinner); otherwise the size the server announces is used.

timeout

Seconds allowed for the whole transfer: a whole number from 1 to 2147483647, default 3600. A transfer slower than 64 bytes a second for 30 seconds is ended before that.

quiet

TRUE, FALSE, or NULL (the default) to follow the session and options.

tty

Draw the live bar (TRUE) or print milestone lines (FALSE); NULL (the default) draws the bar when the console redraws a line in place, as described in Details.

allow_file

Logical, default FALSE: accept a file:// URL (for offline tests).

max_bytes

Most bytes the body may have (default 2 GiB, the transport's ceiling). A body past it, chunked or not, ends the transfer with an error and leaves nothing behind: a caller that expects a small file should say so.

Value

dest, invisibly.

Details

Progress is an animated bar, redrawn in place, when the console can redraw a line: a terminal, or the RStudio, Positron, R.app or RKWard console (never a knitr or Jupyter notebook; the options rmoriebricklayer.dynamic or cli.dynamic, or the environment variable R_CLI_DYNAMIC, override the choice). In the RStudio or Positron console the bar is drawn on stdout, elsewhere on stderr. Otherwise milestone lines go to stderr (every 10 percent, or every 50 MB when the size is unknown), and nothing is shown when quiet. By default output is shown in an interactive session or when options(morie.progress = TRUE) is set, and suppressed by options(morie.quiet = TRUE).

Network: the transfer runs in the package's compiled HTTP client. The URL is checked, its host resolved and pinned, and every redirect is checked again (no switch from https to http; credentials are not passed to another host). Plain http:// is allowed only with options(rmoriebricklayer.allow_http = TRUE). A transfer slower than 64 bytes a second for 30 seconds is abandoned. A file:// URL is copied locally through the same progress display, only with allow_file = TRUE.

Errors: a URL that is not https (or allowed http/file), or that points at a loopback, link-local or private address; headers not a named character vector; timeout below 1 or above 2147483647; max_bytes below 1; a network failure; an HTTP status of 400 or more; a body larger than max_bytes. dest is overwritten.

See also

bricklayer_fetch for a download with a Wayback Machine fallback.

Examples

# offline: a local file through the same routine
src <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
writeLines("hello", src)
dest <- tempfile(fileext = ".txt")
bricklayer_download(paste0("file://", src), dest, quiet = TRUE,
                    allow_file = TRUE)
readLines(dest)
#> [1] "hello"

# the safety checks run before any connection is made
try(bricklayer_download("http://example.org/table.csv", tempfile()))
#> Error : url must be an https:// URL, not http:// ('http://example.org/table.csv'); options(rmoriebricklayer.allow_http = TRUE) admits a trusted plain-http mirror
try(bricklayer_download("https://127.0.0.1/table.csv", tempfile()))
#> Error : url points at a local or private address ('https://127.0.0.1/table.csv'): refused (a local or private address (127.0.0.1))
try(bricklayer_download(paste0("file://", src), tempfile()))
#> Error : url must be an https:// URL, not file:// ('file:///tmp/Rtmp88UIXI/file1e04327e40a0.txt'); options(rmoriebricklayer.allow_http = TRUE) admits a trusted plain-http mirror

# a real download needs the network
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
bricklayer_download("https://www.ontario.ca/some/open-data/table.csv",
                    "table.csv", max_bytes = 50e6)
} # }
